title: Justinian’s Corpus Juris Civilis
summary: Justinian’s commissions compile Roman law into a corpus that later Europe would rediscover.
body: The Digest, Code, and Institutes are legal monuments. Justinian’s wars and the later plague belong to the same ambitious, costly reign. Editorial draft for this timeline, not a substitute for specialist literature.

sources.name: Humfress, in The Cambridge Companion to the Age of Justinian
